title: Performance Measures and Attribution
august: Jensen's alpha, Sharpe and other metrics theory.

maps.tested: The discrimination is when each measure applies: total-risk versus systematic-risk denominators, single-portfolio versus many-portfolio contexts, not the arithmetic. One recall flags the Sharpe question as 'a bit hard'.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'Sharpe ratio (this was bit hard)'; 'Mvar, vol, rf is given, calculate Sharpe ratio'; 'IR, alpha'; 'portfolio manager asset allocation and selection attributes', i.e. performance attribution split into allocation and selection effects. Grinold's fundamental law and the maximum attainable information ratio (LO 85.d) sit alongside.

vardeezReading: IM-7: Very Important, with the note "Time-Weighted vs Dollar-Weighted Returns, M2 Calculation and Style Analysis which is Last LO in this chapter". IM-3: Very Important, with the note "1. Grinold's Fundamental Law (IC, Breadth, IR) 2) Calculation of FAMA French Model using SMB, HML (Pls know this very well) and 3) Style Analysis".

selectors.name: Sharpe ratio, harder form (with M-squared)
selectors.what: Sharpe ratio = (portfolio return - risk-free rate) / sigma_P, paired with M-squared: weight w = sigma_M / sigma_P in the portfolio and T-bills, M2 = r_P* - r_M = (S_P - S_M) x sigma_M. Also asks why Sharpe is the wrong lens for one of many subportfolios (Treynor fits there).
selectors.theory: Sharpe rewards excess return per unit of total volatility and is the slope of the capital allocation line; M2 gives the same ranking as Sharpe read as a return after mixing with T-bills to match the index volatility; Sharpe suits a portfolio that is the entire risky investment, not one piece of many.

selectors.name: Sharpe ratio chained from marginal VaR
selectors.what: A Sharpe ratio calculation in which marginal VaR, volatility and the risk-free rate are given and the inputs must be chained through to the ratio: Sharpe = (return - rf) / sigma.
selectors.theory: How an excess return per unit of total risk is built from risk inputs given in other forms, and that the risk-free rate must be deducted from the return, not left in.

selectors.name: Jensen's alpha and information ratio
selectors.what: Jensen's alpha = r_P - [rf + beta_P (r_M - rf)], plain or with a multifactor benchmark; information ratio = alpha / sigma(e_P), alpha per unit of residual (tracking) risk.
selectors.theory: Alpha is the return above the risk-adjusted benchmark and is necessary but not sufficient to beat the index; the IR measures alpha per unit of nonsystematic risk and drives the Sharpe improvement when an active portfolio is mixed with the benchmark; a naive alpha of r_P - r_M assumes beta of 1.

selectors.name: Attribution: allocation and selection effects
selectors.what: Performance attribution against the bogey: asset allocation = sum of (w_P - w_B) x r_index; security selection = sum of w_P x (r_P - r_index); together they equal the excess return. Within a class, sector allocation plus security selection is multiplied by the class weight before entering the total.
selectors.theory: Allocation uses benchmark class returns and weight differences, selection uses portfolio weights and the return gap within each class; the two effects add to the total excess return over the bogey.

selectors.name: Grinold's fundamental law, maximum IR
selectors.what: Maximum attainable information ratio IR = IC x sqrt(BR), with IC the correlation of forecasts with actual returns and BR the number of independent bets; forward, or solved for IC or breadth.
selectors.theory: More independent bets and better forecasts raise the attainable IR; the law ignores transaction costs and trading restrictions, assumes independent bets and an IC that does not fall as assets grow, and rests on mean-variance utility.

selectors.name: Which measure suits which use
selectors.what: Matching Sharpe, Treynor and the information ratio to the decision context: Sharpe when the portfolio is the entire risky investment, Treynor for one subportfolio among many, the information ratio for an active portfolio mixed with the benchmark, and what sits in each denominator.

selectors.name: Time-weighted versus dollar-weighted return
selectors.what: Distinguishing the time-weighted (geometric, equal weight per period) return from the dollar-weighted return (IRR of the cash flows), which one judges the manager and which reflects the client's experience, and computing them from a short cash-flow example.

selectors.name: Style analysis
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Style analysis' (IM-7 e, IM-3 f; 'the last LO in this chapter')
selectors.what: Sharpe's style analysis: regressing fund returns on asset-class indexes with non-negative coefficients summing to 100%; reading the weights as the style mix, R-squared as the share of variability explained by style, and the intercept as the average return from security selection.
